Claire / team — dug into the traces and sketched a technical tradeoff comparison and a concrete contingency plan. Long but wanted to be explicit.

Short tl;dr:
- L4 is excellent for high QPS, low-cost embedding throughput; it compresses cost per token but lacks the memory for large KV caches / 32k contexts and has higher variance on edge latency for long context ops.
- A100 (80GB) is the middle ground: large memory for KV/prefix cache and good throughput for batched long-context inference with predictable latency; cheaper than H100 for many batched workloads.
- H100 delivers best-single-instance latency and best scaling for very large-context transformer ops (and some fused kernels). Use for strict tail-SLOs and minimal batching.

Concrete numbers from our internal benchmarks (typical, will vary by model):
- Embeddings: L4   ->  ~2.5–3x cost-efficiency vs A100 for high-batch embeddings; per-GPU throughput for the embedding model we tested: ~120k vectors/min (batched)
- Long-context chat (32k): A100 80GB -> ~450 tokens/sec (stable); H100 -> ~650 tokens/sec but 1.6–2x cost per token vs A100 when both are fully utilized
- Latency tail: H100 95th ~90–120ms for short-sessions (<2k tokens) vs A100 95th ~130–200ms depending on batching and concurrency

Design for NovaMed pilot (recommended architecture):
1) Dedicated A100 pool (primary): sized to handle 95% of interactive summarization load with KV/prefix caching enabled. This gives predictable latency for long contexts and a straightforward quantization / kernel path.
2) L4 fleet (throughput fleet): attach as a separate capacity tier for high-throughput embedding batches. Autoscale aggressively (stateless) during business-hour spikes. Use batching knob to maximize throughput per GPU.
3) H100 hot-pool (latency guard): small reserved capacity (2–4 GPUs) that serves low-batch, latency-critical requests and acts as a fallback when A100 queueing would push tail beyond SLA. Attach auto-fallback routing policy: if predicted finish time on A100 > SLO, route to H100 if capacity available.
4) Contingency (burst/spot): pre-warmed A100 standby nodes (kept at low utilization) and pre-warmed L4 instances for sudden embedding spikes; prefer horizontal scaling to avoid long cold-starts.

Caching and KV strategy (critical to reduce cost):
- Prefix caching: for many of the summarization workflows, the clinical forms include repeated system and context prompts. Cache those KV states at the route-level; can cut repeated autoregression token compute by ~25–45% depending on reuse.
- Short-term memcache for embeddings: keep recent embeddings in a hot Redis layer to avoid repeat generation for near-duplicate docs.

Operational notes and fallbacks:
- Routing policy: prioritize A100 for long-context requests until we hit queue depth threshold (configurable) then fail over to H100 (if available) or degrade to a best-effort L4 path (with a notice sent to the app).
- Cost hedge: set a burst cap so L4 autoscaling cannot exceed a predictable monthly ceiling; if burst cap reached, respond with a soft error + retry guidance.

Example sizing (pilot assumptions from traces):
- Summarization: 6 concurrent long-context sessions average -> provision 6x A100 slots (allowing for KV cache memory headroom) -> translate to 2 A100 80GB GPUs (multi-model packing assumed) for pilot of this size.
- Embeddings: sustained 200 r/s with 800 r/s peaks -> 4x L4 GPUs baseline with autoscale to 12 during peaks (stateless batching).
- H100: reserve 2 GPUs as hot-pool.

Risks / notes:
- If NovaMed increases context lengths frequently to >32k or moves to models with very different kernel profiles, we may need to shift more weight to H100.
- Quantization: consider int8/4 quant for A100 where model supports it; keeps memory footprint down and increases packing. H100 may give less quantization benefit for some kernels.

I'll put these recommendations into the SKU spreadsheet and annotate estimated monthly cost deltas. Happy to run a live perf test with your sample traces if you want numbers tuned to your exact model.

—Ben

Team — quick procurement/ops note to include in the write-up for Claire/procurement:

1) Recommended commit tiers (pilot -> production):
   - Pilot (30 days): small reserved A100 pool (2 GPUs) + 4 L4 on-demand with autoscale -> evaluate utilization and tail-SLOs
   - Prod (initial commit): commit to 6x A100 80GB + 8x L4 + 2x H100 hot-pool (3–6 month minimum) to get favorable pricing and capacity guarantees

2) SLA exceptions: NovaMed needs <150ms tail for some requests; standard Dedicated SLA covers uptime but tail-SLOs need explicit carveouts and an SLO-backed credit mechanism. See attached SLA-exception-request.docx — this is the template we'll use to request a product SLA addendum from legal.

3) Operationally: we should include a route-level autoscaler configuration in the RA (runbook) that describes queue thresholds, fallback routing, and warm-pool policies. Laura / AE: we should confirm whether NovaMed expects dedicated IP/tenant isolation at day-1. If yes, include dedicated VPC onboarding steps.

I'll review costs with Finance after Ben finalizes the estimated spreadsheets.
